description: Configuration for Fathom, the terminal UI that keeps a human's mental model of a codebase a coding agent is writing. Values are layered: command-line flags > environment variables (FATHOM_*, segments joined by __) > repo fathom.toml > user config > built-in defaults, and every effective value is explainable with `fathom config explain`. GENERATED from src/recommender/config/schema.py by `python3 -m recommender.config schema --write`; do not edit by hand.

api.description: Which paths' exports the rest of the world compiles against, and how loudly a change to them speaks. A workspace of nine crates usually has two whose `pub` items are somebody else's contract, and a breaking change reported in the third is noise - the ignore and private sets are how the owner says which ones count, and `api.track_tests` is where the built-in answer to `is this a test file?` (`e3.12`) can be overruled. Reading the source is `[extract]`'s business; this table is the claim about the repository.

ignore.description: Paths whose exports are not tracked at all - a test tree, a vendored directory, the binary crate nobody imports. A stated exclusion: ignored paths are counted and named in the report, so "the surface did not change" always says how much of the repository it declined to look at. `e3.7`.

max_items_per_package.description: The ceiling on how many public items one package carries. Above it the package says it is truncated rather than growing without limit: a bound the report states, not a switch that turns a feature off. `e3.7`.

mode.description: How loudly an API change speaks. `off` examines nothing and says so - deliberately a different answer from "examined and clean", because a gate has to tell those apart; `warn` reports without deciding an exit code; `deny` makes a breaking change the `fathom check` violation exit (7). The volume, never the facts. `e3.7`.

package.description: A path prefix pinned to a package name, written `sdk/ts = @acme/sdk`, for directories whose manifest is missing or says something different from what the reviewer means by a package. Longest match wins, and the report names the rule that decided a package. `e3.7`.

private.description: Packages that exist and are published to nobody. Their surface is still extracted and still reported; the semver recommendation says *internal* instead of proposing a version bump for a package no caller can install. `e3.7`.

track_tests.description: Whether test files are public surface, and `False` is a decision rather than an omission. Nothing outside a test file can import it, cargo compiles `tests/` as a crate nothing can `use`, and the only importer of `tests/test_x.py` is the runner that collects it by name - so renaming one is maintenance, not a breaking removal (`e3.12` / `reco-u1i`, which is what happened when this check called a Python test function a removed public item). The rule is each language's own (cargo's `tests/`, pytest's `test_*.py`, Go's `_test.go`, Maven's `src/test/java`, RSpec's `spec/`); declined paths are counted and named in every report, and `True` puts them back for a repository whose tests are the published artefact.

attribution.description: Who wrote a commit: the registry of known agents, the marker table, and the confidence bar below which Fathom prints `?` instead of guessing. Every value here is handed to the classifier as data — no crate below the CLI opens this file.

agents.description: The registry of known agents: one entry per agent id, holding lower-cased substrings of an author, committer or trailer identity. Entries are added to the built-in registry (codex, copilot, claude, devin, aider, …), because a registry that silently dropped an entry would relabel that agent's commits as human work. An entry whose patterns match decides the agent the label names.

^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$.description: The registry of known agents: one entry per agent id, holding lower-cased substrings of an author, committer or trailer identity. Entries are added to the built-in registry (codex, copilot, claude, devin, aider, …), because a registry that silently dropped an entry would relabel that agent's commits as human work. An entry whose patterns match decides the agent the label names.
x-fathom-open: a known-agent id from the attribution registry (`e4.1`): the name the label prints as the agent

ambiguous_below.description: Below this confidence the verdict is `unknown` with the reason printed, rather than the weak label the evidence would have supported. The built-in 0.50 prices the weakest rung (`identity`) exactly at the bar, so nothing is demoted until a repository asks for it.

markers.description: Substrings that make an identity look agent-shaped (`jane@copilot.example`), added to the built-in table. A marker that matches only inside an address's *domain* is read as ambiguity, not as an agent, because `jane@assistant.fr` is a person at a hosting name.

trust_committer.description: Whether the committer counts as evidence when the author does not: a bot that applies a human's change moves the committer and leaves the author alone. A repository whose CI commits everything should turn this off rather than read every episode as `agent`.

blast.description: How far the blast-radius walk goes before it declares a partial, the confidence attached to each basis, and the path-heuristic weights that decide what counts as reached.

confidence.description: Confidence attached to a blast answer that came from a module graph. Not 1.0: a graph is built by an extractor, and spike `s1` measured declarations a program wrote (Rust macros, Python decorators) that no extractor can enumerate. `e2.10`.

graph.description: Confidence attached to a blast answer that came from a module graph. Not 1.0: a graph is built by an extractor, and spike `s1` measured declarations a program wrote (Rust macros, Python decorators) that no extractor can enumerate. `e2.10`.

heuristic.description: Confidence attached to a blast answer built from path heuristics instead of a graph. The plan asks for the reduced confidence to be *stated*; this is the number it states. `e2.10`.

narrow_census.description: Multiplier applied to a heuristic blast answer when the caller lent no file inventory, so the only paths the heuristics could see were the episode's own. A reach computed from a world of twelve files may not claim the confidence of one computed from four thousand. `e2.10`.

heuristic.description: Heuristic weight: a candidate in the changed file's own directory - the strongest path signal there is, because same folder means same imports in every layout that has folders. `e2.10`.

min_score.description: Heuristic score a candidate must reach to be counted as reached. This floor is what stops 'it is in the same repository' being a blast radius. `e2.10`.

package_prefix.description: Heuristic weight: everything under the changed file's top-level package (two directory levels). Cheap and wide, which is why it normally sits under `blast.heuristic.min_score` and only counts when nothing stronger fired. `e2.10`.

same_directory.description: Heuristic weight: a candidate in the changed file's own directory - the strongest path signal there is, because same folder means same imports in every layout that has folders. `e2.10`.

sibling_directory.description: Heuristic weight: the files in the changed file's parent directory. Weaker than same-directory on purpose - a parent's own files are neighbours, not dependents. `e2.10`.

test_pair.description: Heuristic weight: the test file that covers a changed source file, or the source a changed test covers, matched by naming convention only. `e2.10`.

hops.description: Rings counted *beyond* the direct one: the direct ring is always counted, so the default of 1 answers 'direct + one hop' and 0 answers 'direct only'. Anything further out is a stated partial, never a silent stop. `e2.10`.

max_candidates.description: Candidate paths examined before the heuristic walk stops. Stopping is a stated partial naming how many paths were not looked at, so the cost guard shows up in the answer instead of being a silent truncation. `e2.10`.

max_rows.description: Blast rows printed per ring before the remainder is counted and named. `e2.10`.

cache.description: The class-R budget. Defaults come from the size class, not from a magic number.

budget.description: LRU ceiling on class-R cache rows and their blobs (ADR-004 §11).

mib.description: LRU ceiling on class-R cache rows and their blobs (ADR-004 §11).

protect_recent_minutes.description: ADR-004 §8.6's protection set, as a recency window: a cache row used inside this window is not evicted, however cold the rest of the table is. The default is a day, because a repository someone is looking at today is a session and not a cold row. Zero disables the protection, which is what a CI job that wants the budget honoured exactly wants.

card.description: The one-screen answer per episode. Row caps, how loud a finding has to be to earn an attention row, and one switch per section - because a repository narrowing its own card is a different thing from a card quietly losing a question, and the card prints which happened.

attention.description: Lightest severity that earns an attention row. Findings below it are still counted and the count is printed, because 'nothing here' and 'nothing loud' are different claims. `e2.10`.

severity.description: Lightest severity that earns an attention row. Findings below it are still counted and the count is printed, because 'nothing here' and 'nothing loud' are different claims. `e2.10`.

max_evidence.description: Evidence lines printed under a figure. Everything behind the link is in `--json` and in the view the link names, whether or not the card had room for it. `e2.10`.

max_figures.description: Figure rows printed per section before the remainder is counted and named. A cap that names its remainder, never a truncation without a trace: the audit fails a card that trimmed a figure in silence. `e2.10`.

max_findings.description: Attention rows before the rest are counted rather than cut. Ordering is severity, then source section, then name, so the same rows come out twice. `e2.10`.

sections.description: Print the what-changed section: semantic counts after `e2.2` folds reformat, generated and lockfile churn, plus the path-class mix. `e2.10`.

attention.description: Print the attention roll-up: the findings the other sections raised, in severity order, each with the evidence that put it there. `e2.10`.

blast.description: Print the blast-radius section: direct dependents plus a one-hop estimate, with the basis and the confidence beside the count. `e2.10`.

dependencies.description: Print the dependency section from `e2.6`'s delta. Switching it off is a stated omission on the card, not a section that vanishes. `e2.10`.

surface.description: Print the non-code surface section: env, flags, migrations, CI, IaC and container findings with the operator actions they require. `e2.10`.

tests.description: Print the test-surface section: test versus production lines with their absolutes, named cases, and the coverage findings. Never a coverage percentage. `e2.10`.

what.description: Print the what-changed section: semantic counts after `e2.2` folds reformat, generated and lockfile churn, plus the path-class mix. `e2.10`.

where.description: Print the where-it-landed section: directories touched, lines and files that moved, the structural story and the churn band, with the census basis. `e2.10`.

state.description: Decimal places on every ratio, share and confidence the card prints. One code path formats them, so `0.615` cannot be `0.62` in two sections of one card. `e2.10`.

digits.description: Decimal places on every ratio, share and confidence the card prints. One code path formats them, so `0.615` cannot be `0.62` in two sections of one card. `e2.10`.

check.description: What `fathom check` enforces in this repository, and where the run turns red. One table holds the layout version, the gate's volume, the threshold that exits 7, each check's severity and each family's own numbers. It is per-repository and it is read strictly: a value that will not parse, a key this build does not know, or a layout version it cannot read is a refusal (exit 5), never a defaulted pass — a gate that half-reads a policy is a gate that passes what it never looked at.

api_files.description: How many blobs the api check may read per revision. Hitting the cap **blocks** the check rather than shortening the answer, because a clean surface over a corpus this run did not read is the silent pass this ticket exists to refuse. `e6.6`.

base.description: Default far end of the range when `--base` is not given - usually `origin/main`. Empty means the built-in default `HEAD~1`, which the run names out loud rather than pretending it was chosen. A base the clone does not have is a stated `blocked` check, not a pass. `e6.6`.

dependencies.description: A dependency that is direct now and was not before. `e6.6`.

downgrade.description: A direct dependency that moved backwards - which is usually a revert nobody labelled as one. `e6.6`.

forbid.description: Package names that may not arrive at all, exact or glob, each refusal an `error`. The one dependency knob that is a decision rather than a question. `e6.6`.

major_change.description: A direct dependency whose leading version component moved. Crude on purpose - the gate reads what the lockfile wrote and never resolves a version - and stated as crude. `e6.6`.

new_direct.description: A dependency that is direct now and was not before. `e6.6`.

new_source.description: A new registry, git URL, vendored or path source appearing in the range: the shape a supply-chain change takes. `e6.6`.

fail_on.description: The severity at or above which the run fails with exit 7 (`CHECK_VIOLATIONS`). `never` makes the gate a reporter: everything is listed, nothing is decided. This is the only threshold that decides an exit code, which is why the scorecard and the risk score refuse to own one. `e6.6`.

head.description: Default near end of the range. `e6.6`.

ignore.description: Silenced findings, as `<check>` or `<check>:<rule>`. Silencing is not deleting: every format counts silenced findings and prints an example, so a green run can be asked what it did not show. A pattern naming no check is refused at load. `e6.6`.

max_episodes.description: How many episodes the episode-shaped checks read from a range at all. Past it the run says so instead of quietly sampling half a release. `e6.6`.

max_findings.description: How many findings one check lists before the rest are folded into a count. The counts stay whole and the report says `n of m listed`, so the bound changes the list and never the verdict. `e6.6`.

mode.description: The volume of the whole gate. `off` reports and decides nothing - and says so in every output, so a switched-off gate never reads as a clean one; `warn` reports findings and exits 0; `deny` lets a finding at or above `check.fail_on` exit 7. `e6.6`.

require.description: Checks that must actually run. A required check that cannot run - no index, no module graph, a base missing from a shallow clone, a binary built without the feature - fails the gate instead of noting itself skipped. `e6.6`.

risk.description: The `e4.4` score at or over which an episode counts as high-risk for the sign-off check. Not `risk.tau`: `tau` routes a queue, and the pipeline recipe is explicit that a routing knob must not become a merge threshold. This one is paired with *and nobody signed it off*, which makes it a claim about the review. `e6.6`.

threshold.description: The `e4.4` score at or over which an episode counts as high-risk for the sign-off check. Not `risk.tau`: `tau` routes a queue, and the pipeline recipe is explicit that a routing knob must not become a merge threshold. This one is paired with *and nobody signed it off*, which makes it a claim about the review. `e6.6`.

risk_episodes.description: How many episodes of the range the risk scorer may read, newest first - `fathom why`'s cost times a range is a budget, and a bounded read says it was bounded. `e6.6`.

severity.description: How loudly a new violation of `[layering]` speaks in the gate. `off` is a stated choice and is printed as one. `e6.6`.

api.description: How loudly a breaking change to a tracked public surface speaks. Indeterminate changes - the ones a scope that cannot be enumeration forces - are reported at `note` whatever this is, because they are a statement about the reader's knowledge and not about the change. `e6.6`.

cycles.description: How loudly a cycle this range introduced speaks. Baselined cycles are debt and are never news here, whatever this says. `e6.6`.

dependencies.description: The default volume for the dependency families, each of which `[check.dependencies]` may set on its own. `e6.6`.

layering.description: How loudly a new violation of `[layering]` speaks in the gate. `off` is a stated choice and is printed as one. `e6.6`.

sign-off.description: How loudly a high-risk episode with no human sign-off speaks. The pair matters: the gate objects to the missing review, never to the size of the change. `e6.6`.

tests.description: How loudly new logic without tests beside it speaks. `e6.6`.
Added logic lines below which the untested-logic check does not fire. Below this, missing tests are a review comment; above it they are a gate. `e6.6`.

min_new_lines.description: Added logic lines below which the untested-logic check does not fire. Below this, missing tests are a review comment; above it they are a gate. `e6.6`.

min_tested_ratio.description: Test lines added as a share of logic lines added, under which the check fires. Counted from the same index rows `fathom why` prints, so the arithmetic is checkable against a verb that already existed. `e6.6`.

version.description: Which `[check]` layout the file is written in. A declaration above what this build reads is **refused**, not partly understood: a policy enforced halfway is a gate that passes things it never looked at. `e6.6`.

deps.description: Which ecosystems' manifests and lockfiles are parsed, and what the dependency-risk answer does with them: the advisory cache and its freshness bars, the licence matrix, and how hard provenance looks for the episode that asked for a package. Consent to reach the network is not here - it is `privacy.advisories`, because a cloned repository must not be able to grant it.

advisories.description: Whether the dependency-risk card answers advisories at all. Off, the card still renders and says advisories were switched off — an enrichment that vanishes silently is a worse answer than one with a line in it. `e2.7`.

cache.description: Where cached OSV responses live, relative to the repository root. A missing file is an answer with a stated partial in it, never an error. `e2.7`.

ecosystems.description: Ecosystem names, in OSV's spelling, that advisories are asked about. `extend`, so a repository naming its vendored registry does not drop the eight everyone else gets. A package in an ecosystem not listed is reported as not checked, never as clean. `e2.7`.

enabled.description: Whether the dependency-risk card answers advisories at all. Off, the card still renders and says advisories were switched off — an enrichment that vanishes silently is a worse answer than one with a line in it. `e2.7`.

max_age_hours.description: Age past which a cached entry is `stale`: still used, and labelled as used. A clean answer with no age on it is a claim with no date. `e2.7`.

max_packages.description: How many packages one episode's refresh will look up, with the remainder printed as 'not checked (cap reached)' rather than silently dropped. Bounds the refresh that a lockfile rewrite turned into four hundred requests. `e2.7`.

mode.description: `cache` reads the local cache and never fetches; `refresh` may fetch, but only with `privacy.advisories` consent as well; `offline` does not read the cache either and says so on the card. Default `cache`, because 'zero network calls by default' is a default *mode*, not a default flag. `e2.7`.

stale_limit_hours.description: Age past which the answer stops claiming 'no advisories found' and says 'not checked recently' instead — the tense change is the whole point, because a seven-week-old clean result is not a clean result. Must be at or above `max_age_hours`; the schema cannot say that across two keys, so the analyzer refuses the pair. `e2.7`.

timeout_ms.description: Per-request budget for a consented refresh — a bound on blocking, which exists because a lookup that can hang is a lookup that blocks episode rendering, and `e2.7` forbids that. `e2.7`.

card.description: Findings printed on the card. Past the cap they are counted in the summary line rather than hidden: a card that quietly omits the eleventh violation is worse than a long one. `e2.7`.

max_evidence.description: Evidence lines printed per finding on the card. `0` prints kinds only, for a reviewer who wants the census first and the evidence on demand. `e2.7`.

max_findings.description: Findings printed on the card. Past the cap they are counted in the summary line rather than hidden: a card that quietly omits the eleventh violation is worse than a long one. `e2.7`.

ecosystems.description: Ecosystems whose manifests and lockfiles are parsed (the parser set is `e2.5`). Enabling one here never enables a network call.

findings.description: The repository now asks for a package by name that it did not ask for before: the row that carries the answer, and the reason this card exists. `e2.7`.

advisory_cache_missing.description: There was no cache to read. The card renders anyway: advisories are an enrichment, never a precondition of the answer. `e2.7`.

advisory_cache_stale.description: The cache is older than `max_age_hours`, or past `stale_limit_hours`. A stale cache is still a usable cache; this finding says which one it is looking at. `e2.7`.

advisory_critical.description: Cached OSV data reports a critical advisory for this package at this version. Off, this card could not raise a critical finding at all, which is why it is on and why the switch is stated rather than assumed. `e2.7`.

advisory_fix_available.description: An advisory names a fixed version at or after the installed one, so the action is a bump rather than an argument, and the row names the version. `e2.7`.

advisory_high.description: Cached OSV data reports a high-severity advisory for this package at this version. `e2.7`.

advisory_low.description: Cached OSV data reports a low-severity advisory. Loud enough to see, not loud enough to compete with the one that has a fix. `e2.7`.

advisory_moderate.description: Cached OSV data reports a moderate advisory — including the ones upstream left unseverity, which are printed as unseverity and never as nothing. `e2.7`.

advisory_unchecked.description: Packages this answer did not check, grouped by reason — no cached entry, ecosystem not asked about, cap reached. 'No advisories found' is only honest next to this line. `e2.7`.

intent_not_captured.description: The introducing episode is known and its intent is not, or only a prompt digest is. A digest proves a request happened; it does not say what it was. `e2.7`.

license_added_to_set.description: A licence id is newly present in what this repository ships, violation or not: the id, and the package that brought it. `e2.7`.

license_denied.description: The licence is one this repository's policy refuses for the layer that now asks for it. The finding names the edge path, because 'who asked' is the half a reviewer can act on. `e2.7`.

license_drift.description: An existing package's declared licence moved between the two revisions — same name, different permission. Nobody reviewed a relicence unless this row says so. `e2.7`.

license_flagged.description: The licence is allowed but its matrix cell is `warn`: permitted, and still a decision nobody has made out loud. `e2.7`.

license_unknown.description: Nothing declared a licence, so policy cannot be evaluated. A stated partial, never a pass. `e2.7`.

new_direct_dependency.description: The repository now asks for a package by name that it did not ask for before: the row that carries the answer, and the reason this card exists. `e2.7`.

new_source.description: A registry, git URL or vendored tree this repository had never resolved from. The package may be innocent; the origin is what is new, and origins are where supply chains are actually attacked. `e2.7`.

provenance_unknown.description: Nothing readable names the episode that introduced a new direct dependency. Printed as the answer — 'not recorded', plus what would fill it — because a blank line reads as 'nothing to see'. `e2.7`.

vcs_source.description: Resolved from git/svn/hg instead of a registry: no immutable version, no registry signature, and a commit as the reviewable unit — a different question than the one a registry version answers. `e2.7`.

license.description: Licence ids refused wherever they appear, matrix included — a named refusal outranks a class. `extend`, so adding SSPL cannot be done by rewriting the built-in list and losing AGPL on the way. `e2.7`.

card.description: Licence rows printed on the card before the remainder is counted and the verb that lists them is named. A cap on rows is not a deletion: the render audit fails the card if a violation goes missing rather than going to the 'N more' line. `e2.7`.

max_rows.description: Licence rows printed on the card before the remainder is counted and the verb that lists them is named. A cap on rows is not a deletion: the render audit fails the card if a violation goes missing rather than going to the 'N more' line. `e2.7`.

deny.description: Licence ids refused wherever they appear, matrix included — a named refusal outranks a class. `extend`, so adding SSPL cannot be done by rewriting the built-in list and losing AGPL on the way. `e2.7`.

ignore_dev.description: Skip development-only dependencies when evaluating licence policy. Off by default: a copyleft test fixture that ships in the wheel is still shipped, and the finding nobody expected is still the finding. `e2.7`.

library_layers.description: Which declared layers count as the library layer: the layer whose licences propagate to whoever links it, and therefore the layer the matrix is strict about. Read against `layers.*`. `e2.7`.

network_copyleft.description: Copyleft whose trigger includes offering the code as a service, so 'we only run it' does not escape it. Denied in every layer by default; a repository that has taken advice can move a cell to `warn`. `e2.7`.

network_copyleft_elsewhere.description: What network copyleft may do outside the library layer. See the row above: both cells are `deny` because the class is the reason, not the layer. `e2.7`.

network_copyleft_in_library.description: What network copyleft may do in the library layer. Both network-copyleft cells default to `deny`, because the trigger is how software is *offered*, which no layering decision changes. `e2.7`.

permissive.description: Ids treated as permissive: allowed everywhere, and still counted when one is newly present in what the repository ships. Taught by table rather than baked in, so an unusual-but-fine id is a config edit and not a fork. `e2.7`.

strong_copyleft.description: Whole-work copyleft. Whether that is fatal depends on whether the distributor is the library or an application built from it — which is why this is a class with a matrix row and not a deny list. `e2.7`.

strong_copyleft_elsewhere.description: What strong copyleft may do outside the library layer — `warn`, because a GPL CLI in the composition layer is usually a decision someone made on purpose, and the finding is there to have it confirmed. `e2.7`.

strong_copyleft_in_library.description: What strong copyleft may do in the library layer. `deny` by default: linking it from a library hands the obligation to every downstream, which is not a decision a dependency bump gets to make silently. `e2.7`.

unknown_layer_policy.description: How to treat a licence id nobody's table knows. `strict`: an unknown obligation is reported as a stated partial and never as a pass — 'no violation found' about a licence nobody read is the worst thing this tool can say. `e2.7`.

weak_copyleft.description: File-level copyleft: the obligation attaches to the file that carries it, so a library may ship these and an application usually only has to say so. That is a matrix cell, not a fact about MPL. `e2.7`.

weak_copyleft_elsewhere.description: What file-level copyleft may do outside the library layer. `allow`: quiet enough not to compete with the finding that matters. `e2.7`.

weak_copyleft_in_library.description: What file-level copyleft may do in the library layer: allowed, and printed, because MPL-in-a-library is fine right up until someone ships a modification. `e2.7`.

provenance.description: Report an unknown intent as the finding `intent-not-captured` when the introducing episode is known and its reason is not. `e2.7`.

agent_counts_as_intent.description: Let attribution ('agent codex') stand in for intent. Off, and it should stay off: who executed the change is not who asked for it, and turning this on makes `intent: not recorded` impossible to ever see. `e2.7`.

card.description: Provenance rows printed on the card before the remainder is counted and named. `e2.7`.

max_rows.description: Provenance rows printed on the card before the remainder is counted and named. `e2.7`.

intent_sources.description: Which recorded intent sources may be printed as the answer. Evidence from a source listed here is quoted with its source and its confidence; evidence from one not listed is reported as existing-but-not-allowed, because unreviewed text silently used as an explanation is the failure this list exists to prevent. `e2.7`.

min_confidence.description: Minimum confidence for an intent to be printed as the answer rather than as a guess — and a guess is still printed, labelled, rather than dropped. Inferred evidence carries low confidence, so raising this mostly produces more guesses. `e2.7`.

require_intent.description: Report an unknown intent as the finding `intent-not-captured` when the introducing episode is known and its reason is not. `e2.7`.

search_previous_episodes.description: Look through recorded introductions from earlier episodes when the episode under review did not add the package. The question is usually asked weeks after the answer was written. `e2.7`.

churn.description: Episodes that must have edited one region before `churn_loop` calls it a loop, and how far back it looks (four times this). Two episodes touching a function is a hard bug; four is a story. Ships disabled until `e4.3a` measures it. `e4.3`.

min_episodes.description: Episodes that must have edited one region before `churn_loop` calls it a loop, and how far back it looks (four times this). Two episodes touching a function is a hard bug; four is a story. Ships disabled until `e4.3a` measures it. `e4.3`.

copy.description: Consecutive new lines that have to match elsewhere for `copy_paste_growth` to call it a copied block. Ships disabled; this is the knob `e4.3a` tunes first, because a table-driven test and a duplicated idea are the same twelve lines. `e4.3`.

min_block_lines.description: Consecutive new lines that have to match elsewhere for `copy_paste_growth` to call it a copied block. Ships disabled; this is the knob `e4.3a` tunes first, because a table-driven test and a duplicated idea are the same twelve lines. `e4.3`.

disable.description: The off switch for a detector, as opposed to `detectors.suppress`'s off switch for a finding: an id here does not run, and its row in every report says `disabled` — so the question 'did it look?' still has an answer. Applied after `detectors.enabled`, so it wins a collision, and it is the same grammar as `--disable-detector` / `--detectors -id`. `e6.7`.

enabled.description: Detectors that run. Unknown detector ids are a warning naming a valid id.

max_findings.description: Findings kept per detector per episode. What the cap hides is counted in the report, never dropped silently. `e4.3`.

rework.description: Line-set overlap (Jaccard, both directions) that makes an episode a revert of an earlier one. Ships disabled: a rebase and a rework are the same bytes. `e4.3`.

min_overlap.description: Line-set overlap (Jaccard, both directions) that makes an episode a revert of an earlier one. Ships disabled: a rebase and a rework are the same bytes. `e4.3`.

shotgun.description: Directory clusters (the first two path segments of each hand-written file) one episode may touch before `shotgun_edit` calls it spread. Ships disabled, and `e3.1`'s module graph is what will make it a real detector. `e4.3`.

min_clusters.description: Directory clusters (the first two path segments of each hand-written file) one episode may touch before `shotgun_edit` calls it spread. Ships disabled, and `e3.1`'s module graph is what will make it a real detector. `e4.3`.

suppress.description: The off switch: a detector id, an exact suppression key, or a glob over keys. Keys are `detector:subject`, printed by every finding, and contain no episode id and no timestamp so a rebase cannot invalidate one. `e4.3`.

todo.description: New `TODO`/`FIXME`/`todo!()` markers before `todo_debt` speaks. `0` is a real threshold — report the episode that removed one — so unlike a count, zero is not refused. `e4.3`.

min_new.description: New `TODO`/`FIXME`/`todo!()` markers before `todo_debt` speaks. `0` is a real threshold — report the episode that removed one — so unlike a count, zero is not refused. `e4.3`.

untested.description: How big a new public surface has to be before `untested_new_logic` says it owes a test. Below it, a three-line accessor demanding a test is noise the reviewer mutes wholesale. `e4.3`.

min_added_lines.description: How big a new public surface has to be before `untested_new_logic` says it owes a test. Below it, a three-line accessor demanding a test is noise the reviewer mutes wholesale. `e4.3`.

episode.description: Boundary sources in priority order, and the idle gap that ends an episode when nothing better is available.

boundaries.description: Boundary sources, spelled exactly as `episode.boundary_rule` stores them (ADR-003 App. B). `replace`, not `extend`: the *order* is the meaning, and a merged list has no coherent order. The order itself is fixed by ADR-003 §4.5 and is not configurable: a value other than the canonical prefix is named on the run that ignored it. `force_split`/`force_merge` are the supported way to move a boundary.

force_merge.description: Commits that never open an episode, in the same two spellings. Ordered before every other rule, including a turn event: when the human has said two commits are one change, the harness does not overrule them.

force_split.description: Commits that always open a new episode, each named `oid:<prefix>` or `subject:<substring>`. A boundary a human moved is recorded as such on the episode, so the card can say the split was an instruction and not a guess.

time_gap_minutes.description: Idle gap that closes an episode when no stronger boundary source fires.

events.description: Whether a run publishes the analysis lifecycle — what started, what each detector did, what every finding said, how the run ended — as versioned JSONL an external tool can read. Off until the repository says otherwise; the path is `paths.analysis_events`.

enabled.description: Write the analysis event stream when a verb analyses: one versioned JSON object per line, appended to `paths.analysis_events`. Off by default because the product writes no file a repository did not ask for (ADR-001 §4.6); `--events FILE` turns it on for one run, and `--events -` sends the same lines to stderr. `e6.7`.

on.description: Which event kinds to write: an exact kind (`detector.finished`) or a family with `*` (`analysis.*`, `*`). An empty list means every kind. A pattern that will not parse is a notice and the whole stream, never a silent narrowing. `e6.7`.

extract.description: What one file may cost the structural extractor, and how far resolution may chase a re-export chain. Every one of these is a *bound the extractor reports on*, not a switch that turns a feature off: a file refused for size comes back with a reason and its file-level measurement, and a chain cut short comes back with `converged: false` rather than a guess.

complexity.description: Nodes one definition's complexity walk may visit before it stops counting. The complexity numbers are proxies for risk, not a metric with a definition, so the walk is bounded per definition and a truncated count is a note rather than a wrong number. `e3.1`.

max_nodes.description: Nodes one definition's complexity walk may visit before it stops counting. The complexity numbers are proxies for risk, not a metric with a definition, so the walk is bounded per definition and a truncated count is a note rather than a wrong number. `e3.1`.

java.description: How far the Java extractor looks for a dependency that has no `import` statement, which is the one place in the extractor where guessing is a feature: a bare `Builder` in a file means `Builder.java` beside it, and a scan that refuses to say so reports no edge at all. `imports_plus_package` (the default) resolves a bare type reference against the file's own declared package only, with a single-type import shadowing it; `all_type_references` is the wider scan `s1` prototyped, kept because the report publishes the false-positive rate of both (`same_package.scoped` against `same_package.wide`) and because a codebase that never collides type names may want the recall. `e3.1b`, spike `s1` finding 5.

same_package_scan.description: How far the Java extractor looks for a dependency that has no `import` statement, which is the one place in the extractor where guessing is a feature: a bare `Builder` in a file means `Builder.java` beside it, and a scan that refuses to say so reports no edge at all. `imports_plus_package` (the default) resolves a bare type reference against the file's own declared package only, with a single-type import shadowing it; `all_type_references` is the wider scan `s1` prototyped, kept because the report publishes the false-positive rate of both (`same_package.scoped` against `same_package.wide`) and because a codebase that never collides type names may want the recall. `e3.1b`, spike `s1` finding 5.

max_file_bytes.description: Largest file the structural extractor will parse. Above it the file is refused with `too_large` and still gets its file-level measurement - a refused file is never a lost file, which is the difference between a bound and a hole in the graph. `e3.1`.

resolution.description: How many times the corpus may be re-resolved to close a re-export chain. Resolution is a fixpoint, so the bound needs stating and reporting: the output carries `passes_used` and `converged` per file, and a file that did not settle inside this number says so. `e3.1`, spike `s1` finding 6.

max_hops.description: How far one import may follow re-exports before the chain is called truncated. A barrel that re-exports a barrel is normal at two hops and a cycle waiting to happen at forty, so the walk is cut and the cut is counted per file in `resolution.truncated_chains`. `e3.1`, spike `s1` finding 6.

max_passes.description: How many times the corpus may be re-resolved to close a re-export chain. Resolution is a fixpoint, so the bound needs stating and reporting: the output carries `passes_used` and `converged` per file, and a file that did not settle inside this number says so. `e3.1`, spike `s1` finding 6.

ruby.description: How many Ruby files one extraction run may parse, in priority order. Ruby is the one grammar `s1` measured an order of magnitude off the pack (under 1 MiB/s against 11-16 for the others), and the answer is a bound rather than a feature gate: files past the cap come back `scan_budget` with their file-level measurement, exactly as an oversized file comes back `too_large`, so a refused file is still a measured file. 4 000 Ruby files at the measured rate is seconds, and the report's `scan_budget.cost` states that number against the cold-graph budget. `0` means no cap, which is the safe direction for a typo: the failure mode is scanning everything, not an empty graph. `e3.1b`, spike `s1` finding 7.

max_bytes_per_run.description: How many bytes of Ruby one extraction run may parse. The count cap alone binds wrongly on a tree of many small `def`s and never binds on a few generated megabytes, so the cap is both: whichever is spent first stops the run. This is the number that makes Ruby's cost a budget instead of an argument - divide it by the measured rate and you have the worst a cold run may spend on Ruby. `0` means no cap. `e3.1b`.

max_files_per_run.description: How many Ruby files one extraction run may parse, in priority order. Ruby is the one grammar `s1` measured an order of magnitude off the pack (under 1 MiB/s against 11-16 for the others), and the answer is a bound rather than a feature gate: files past the cap come back `scan_budget` with their file-level measurement, exactly as an oversized file comes back `too_large`, so a refused file is still a measured file. 4 000 Ruby files at the measured rate is seconds, and the report's `scan_budget.cost` states that number against the cold-graph budget. `0` means no cap, which is the safe direction for a typo: the failure mode is scanning everything, not an empty graph. `e3.1b`, spike `s1` finding 7.

priority.description: Path prefixes, in order, that decide which Ruby files get read when the per-run cap binds. A run that has to stop early should stop having read what an entry point reaches, hence `lib` and `app` before `spec` and `test` - the opposite of the alphabetical order a directory walk gives you. Files matching no listed prefix are scanned after the listed ones, so this reorders and never drops. `e3.1b`.

graph.description: Directories excluded from the dependency and structure graph.

enabled.description: Write a graph row per revision at index time (`e3.11`, `reco-dlp`). On by default; the two ways off are this key and the index's `--no-graph` flag, and either is a stated choice rather than a fault — every architecture surface says which it was. Off by accident more often than on purpose: this pass is what `fathom architecture`, `check`'s layering and cycle checks, `architecture_delta` and `boundary_scan` read, and none of them can judge anything without it.

ignored_dirs.description: Directory names excluded from the structure/dependency graph entirely.

max_corpus_mib.description: The refusal that stops the graph pass costing more than the index that called it (`e3.11`). One revision's graph needs one structural pass over its whole live source corpus — an import is only resolvable against the set of files that exist, so an unchanged file's edges change when a neighbour appears. Above this size the pass declines, in the report and in `graph.partial`, and touches nothing already stored.

snapshot_cache_mib.description: Ceiling on the revision graphs one lane keeps materialised in memory (`reco-93w`). Eviction is lossless: a snapshot is a fold of durable `graph_delta` rows, so what this buys with memory is not re-walking the anchor chain - `graph.materialise_revision.ms` paid once instead of per navigation. Set it to the number of revisions a session is expected to page through, not to the size of the repository.

window.description: Revisions the index runs the graph pass for in one go, oldest first (`e3.11`). A cost bound and nothing else: two new commits pay for two revisions, and a store that has never had a graph pass says so and works off the tail rather than running a walk a foreground index cannot finish. It raises its hand in the report when it stops short; `graph.chain_full_every` decides separately how often the anchor is repeated.

harness.description: The per-session ingest budget that quarantines a runaway hook stream.

max_bytes_per_session_mib.description: Per-session ingest budget; over quota the session is quarantined rather than trusted (ADR-005 §6.3).

hotspots.description: What the hotspot score is made of: the six metric weights, the knee each saturating curve bends at, the churn window, and how long a new symbol may go unreferenced before it is a candidate. A hotspot is "expensive to change and widely felt", not "bad", and every knob here moves an explainable number rather than switching a report on or off.

dead_code_after.description: How many episodes a newly added symbol may go unreferenced before it is a dead-code candidate. A symbol added last episode has had exactly no chance; below this bar the row is listed as `unverified` rather than claimed as dead. `e3.8`.

duplicate_block_lines.description: How many folded, non-blank lines a repeated block must be to count. Below it `} else {` is a duplicate; `e4.3`'s copy-paste detector uses the same bar for the same reason. `e3.8`.

flags.description: Feature flags this repository declares are ON. It is the only input the gated dead-code class has, and it is a claim the owner wrote down rather than a resolved build configuration: a feature turned on at the command line is invisible to it, and a candidate behind a flag stays `uncertain` either way. `e3.8`.

god_bar.description: The saturated value a metric must reach to count as high for a shape call (god module, hub, sink, giant) and for the churn x complexity quadrant. 0.5 is the knee itself, so every bar in the report is one sentence: at least the published knee. `e3.8`.

ignore.description: Paths excluded from the dead-code sweep - generated code, vendored trees, the fixture corpus. A stated exclusion: the count and the patterns travel with the report, so a candidate list always says how much of the repository it declined to look at. `e3.8`.

knee.description: Where each metric's saturating curve bends: `value = raw / (raw + knee)`, so the raw number equal to the knee is worth exactly 0.5. A published number, printed beside every contribution; `instability` has no knee because it is already a ratio, and setting one there is refused. `e3.8`.

^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$.description: Where each metric's saturating curve bends: `value = raw / (raw + knee)`, so the raw number equal to the knee is worth exactly 0.5. A published number, printed beside every contribution; `instability` has no knee because it is already a ratio, and setting one there is refused. `e3.8`.

min_history.description: How much history the store must hold before a churn column is printed at all. Below it velocity is *unmeasured* and says so, which is the difference between 'this module is not being reworked' and 'this repository is too young to say' - the second is not a zero. `e3.8`.

top.description: How many ranked modules a surface lists. The modules it drops are counted and printed, so 'top 20' is a display choice and not a filter nobody chose. `e3.8`.

weights.description: Per-metric weights of the hotspot score. `deep`: weighting one metric in a repo file does not drop the rest. Values are clamped and never renormalised behind you - the score divides by the weight sum over the metrics actually measured, and prints that denominator. An unknown weight name is a notice naming the six, not a silent no-op. `e3.8`.

^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$.description: Per-metric weights of the hotspot score. `deep`: weighting one metric in a repo file does not drop the rest. Values are clamped and never renormalised behind you - the score divides by the weight sum over the metrics actually measured, and prints that denominator. An unknown weight name is a notice naming the six, not a silent no-op. `e3.8`.

window.description: How many revisions churn velocity is measured over. Thirty episodes is about a working month of an agent-driven repository: long enough that a one-commit spike does not top the table, short enough that a refactor that stopped three weeks ago stops being blamed. `e3.8`.

ingest.description: The size cap: a bigger blob is recorded as oversized, never slurped.

size_cap_mib.description: Largest single blob that enters memory; bigger is recorded as `oversized` with counts, never slurped. The budget face of this knob is `ingest.file_size_cap.mib` — one value, two names, one alias table.

intent.description: What an episode was *for*: the ladder that answers that question (the harness prompt, the `Agent-Intent:` trailer, a `Task:` line, a prompt digest) and how much of the answer is kept. The ladder's ORDER is not configurable, only its membership — an intent a user reordered is an intent nobody can explain, which is the same refusal `[episode] boundaries` and `[attribution]` make.

digest_counts.description: Whether a prompt digest with no text counts as an intent at all. On, the episode reads `digest-only` with the prompt's digest — "a request happened and its text was not captured" is a fact. Off, and such an episode reads `no recorded intent` like any other, which is the honest choice for a repository that would rather not print a hash where a sentence belongs.

max_text_bytes.description: Cap on any one piece of intent text — a prompt, a plan item, a trailer value. A prompt is a paragraph, not a file, and ADR-005 §6.3 forbids file contents crossing this boundary: a harness that echoed a 2 MB prompt into a `UserPromptSubmit` payload would otherwise grow the store by the prompt's size forever. Text that exceeds the cap is kept truncated, and the document says `truncated: true` rather than ending mid-sentence in silence.

plan_cap.description: Plan items kept per episode. The document counts what it dropped instead of quietly losing the tail, because a plan list that silently ends is a plan that was not finished.

scope_cap.description: Declared-scope globs kept per episode. Absolute paths, `..` escapes and anything holding a NUL are refused and named in `scope_rejected`, never normalised into something that reads as a repository-relative glob.

sources.description:
Which rungs of the intent ladder may decide the text, in the published spellings (`hook-prompt`, `hook-intent`, `agent-intent-trailer`, `plan-item`, `task-trailer`, `prompt-digest`). This **replaces** the list rather than extending it: the only interesting use of the key is to turn something off — a repository whose prompts carry names it does not want quoted says `[
"agent-intent-trailer"]` and means exactly that. An entry naming no rung this build reads is a notice, not an error: `review-note` and `manual-note` are spellings `[deps.provenance] intent_sources` already lists, and `e4.6`/`e6.5` are the tickets that would produce them.

keys.description: Per-mode user overrides **only**. The canonical binding table is ADR-006's; conflict detection and the cheatsheet are `e5.4`'s.

overrides.description: User key overrides per mode. Overrides only — `e5.4` detects conflicts and the cheatsheet is generated from the merged table, so neither can lie.

^(?:global|queue|timeline|diff|structure.description: User key overrides per mode. Overrides only — `e5.4` detects conflicts and the cheatsheet is generated from the merged table, so neither can lie.

^[A-Za-z0-9<>^+_,.\\- ]{1,12}$.description: User key overrides per mode. Overrides only — `e5.4` detects conflicts and the cheatsheet is generated from the merged table, so neither can lie.
x-fathom-open: a keymap mode (the canonical table is ADR-006's, `e0.6`)

layering.description: What the declared layers are allowed to depend on: refusals, their exceptions, boundary rules and the cycle rules. `[layers]` says where things live; this says which edges between them are violations. A rule that cannot match anything is refused when the file is read, with the reason, rather than becoming a silent no-op.

allow.description: Exceptions to a refusal, same syntax, and each must be *narrower* than the refusal it excepts - a layer-level refusal with a file-level exception is the shape a real read path takes. An allow that excepts nothing is refused at load: a permission nobody forbade is configuration that enforces nothing. `e3.6`.

forbid.description: Refusals, one per entry, written `src -> dst` where each side is a layer name, a path pattern or `*`. An optional `my-name: ` prefix names the rule in every violation and in every baseline key; without one the rule is named by its own content, so editing the list order cannot move a baseline. `e3.6`.

ignore.description: Path patterns whose outgoing dependencies are not judged - a test tree, a fixtures directory. Same dialect as a `[layers]` pattern. Skipped edges are counted and printed, because an ignored region is a decision and not a clean bill of health. `e3.6`.

max_violations.description: How many violations one report lists before it stops. The bound never changes a number: the report prints how many were found alongside how many are listed. `e3.6`.

mode.description: How loudly the layering rules speak. `off` examines nothing and says so; `warn` reports without deciding an exit code; `deny` makes a new violation the `fathom check` violation exit (7). A baselined violation is debt at every mode - the mode sets the volume, not the facts. `e3.6`.

no_cycle_within_layer.description: Refuse a cycle whose members all sit in one layer: a loop inside a layer means the layer is doing more than one job, which is a different claim from `no_cycles` and gets its own fix hint. `e3.6`.

no_cycles.description: Every dependency cycle between judged modules is a violation. Detection is `e3.5`'s engine - this declares that cycles are refused, and each violation carries the same shortest witness the cycle report prints. `e3.6`.

no_upward.description: Refuse a dependency from a higher-ranked layer to a lower-ranked one, against `layering.order`. Refused at load when the order is empty, because an upward reference with no declared order has no direction. `e3.6`.

only.description: Boundary rules: `target <- the only source that may reach it`, which is why the arrow points the other way from a refusal. Several entries naming the same target are one allow-list, so `db <- api` plus `db <- db` says the api layer and the layer itself may reach it and nothing else may. `e3.6`.

order.description: The layers, bottom first. This is the only thing that makes a reference *upward*: `layering.no_upward` refuses an edge that points at a higher-ranked layer. A layer left out is counted unranked rather than guessed, and a name `[layers]` does not declare is refused at load. `e3.6`.

layers.description: The declared intended architecture: named layers, each a list of path prefixes. An open map, keyed by layer name.

^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$.description: One named layer: the path prefixes that belong to it. `deep`, so a repo file adds a layer without erasing the layers you declared at home.
x-fathom-open: a layer name: lowercase, starts with a letter

mcp.description: Transport, bind address, the write gate (`allow_writes`) and the size one response may reach. The two secrets live here and are user-scoped and redacted — `mcp.auth_token` for a listener, `mcp.approval_token` for a write an agent may make — and a credential a cloned repo could write is a credential already given away.

allow_writes.description: Turn on the two write tools (`mark_reviewed`, `add_review_note`). Off by default, and while off they are absent from `tools/list` rather than present and refusing; while on, every call appends an audit line naming the tool, a digest of its arguments and the outcome (ADR-005 §4.2).

approval_token.description: The secret `mark_reviewed`'s approval token is derived from. User-scoped and redacted like `mcp.auth_token`: a token a clone could write is a token already spent. The token itself is bound to exactly one change, so it cannot walk a queue signing things off.

audit_reads.description: Also write an audit line for the read tools. Off by default: a log of what an agent was curious about is worth having, and it is the operator's call rather than a side effect.

auth_token.description: Bearer token for the HTTP transport. User-scoped and redacted everywhere: a token a clone could write is a token that is already leaked.

bind.description: Listener address, loopback by default. A non-loopback bind is refused without consent: a listener on a shared host is a disclosure, not a convenience.

max_response_bytes.description: The ceiling on one MCP response. A page that will not fit is cut and handed back with `next_cursor`, which makes truncation a fact the caller can act on instead of a mystery.

transport.description: `stdio` opens no socket and is not a network feature (ADR-002 §6.3). `http` is a listener, so it needs `privacy.mcp_http_transport` as well as the compiled-in feature.

meta.description: What the file says about itself, so a newer file is refused rather than half-understood.

config_version.description: Config format this file was written for. A value greater than the running binary's is an error, never a silent partial read.

noise.description: Globs for change that carries no reviewable information. `e0.9` owns the built-in table; this is the user half of it.

builtins_version.description: Version of the *built-in* noise table e0.9 ships. Declared so a taxonomy table bump invalidates the analyzers that read noise (ADR-004 §6).

collapse.description: When *every* file in an episode folded, collapse the episode to one line. This is the 'a reformat-only commit is one line' behaviour, and it is a separate switch so a reviewer can keep per-file fold lines while refusing whole-episode collapses.

noise_only.description: When *every* file in an episode folded, collapse the episode to one line. This is the 'a reformat-only commit is one line' behaviour, and it is a separate switch so a reviewer can keep per-file fold lines while refusing whole-episode collapses.

expand.description: The key that shows a folded change again (AC 4). Configurable because every other key here is configurable, and because the fold lines are *rendered* from this value — a fold that said `[press b]` after you rebind it would be a lie.

globs.description: Path globs treated as noise. `extend`: a repo adds to your list instead of replacing it. A leading `!` re-promotes a path a broader glob demoted.

keep.description: Paths suppression must never fold, whatever the rules say — the reviewer's 'always show me this file' list. Beats every rule, including a repository's own assertion, because the only thing that outranks 'show it' is 'show it'.

suppress.description: Fold a file pair whose token streams are identical — a rustfmt/prettier/gofmt re-layout, not a change. The rule only ever applies to a pair the token model can read; an unreadable pair is never folded. The fold line names the formatter.

generated_churn.description: Fold a generated file whose diff is a stamp line, a re-order of generated entries, or a whole-file regeneration. Deliberately narrower than 'the path is generated': a small edit inside a generated file stays visible, because that is the case where a person edited the generator's output by hand and wants it seen.

lockfile.description: Fold a lockfile to one counted line ('3 dependencies upgraded'). The rule stands aside when the declaring manifest moved too — then the lockfile diff is the dependency decision and is shown.

reformat.description: Fold a file pair whose token streams are identical — a rustfmt/prettier/gofmt re-layout, not a change. The rule only ever applies to a pair the token model can read; an unreadable pair is never folded. The fold line names the formatter.

user_glob.description: Fold a path the layers put in `noise.globs`. A repository adding a glob is asking for its own noise to be folded, not for it to be hidden, so the fold quotes the glob that caught the path.

vendored.description: Fold vendored code (the `vendored` taxonomy class, `e0.9`). A person did not write it and cannot review it here; `fathom config explain --path` says which assertion made a path vendored.

non_code.description: Config, env, flags, migrations and CI — the surfaces a reviewer must be told about even though they are not code.

card.description: Action rows a card prints before it says how many more there are and which verb lists them. A cap that names its remainder, never a truncation without a trace.

max_actions.description: Action rows a card prints before it says how many more there are and which verb lists them. A cap that names its remainder, never a truncation without a trace.

ci.description: Which branch names count as 'the default branch' when deciding whether a trigger means every merge runs this job.

default_branches.description: Which branch names count as 'the default branch' when deciding whether a trigger means every merge runs this job.

escalating_permissions.description: `permissions:` moves that are escalations, in `scope:access` spelling. `write-all` is in the list because it is the escalation that does not name what it escalates.

container.description: Insist that a new or changed base image is pinned by digest. Off in a repository that rebuilds nightly and considers a floating tag the honest answer.

require_digest_pin.description: Insist that a new or changed base image is pinned by digest. Off in a repository that rebuilds nightly and considers a floating tag the honest answer.

env.description: Files whose whole job is to declare environment variables (`.env.example` and friends). A key added here is a key an operator must set; a key added only in code is the same finding with a different location.

committed_globs.description: Files where a *value* is a real value rather than documentation. A `.env` in a repository is usually an accident; a secret-shaped name in one is a rotation.

declaration_globs.description: Files whose whole job is to declare environment variables (`.env.example` and friends). A key added here is a key an operator must set; a key added only in code is the same finding with a different location.

placeholder_values.description: Values that read as documentation (`changeme`, `<secret>`, empty). Compared case- insensitively: this list is what keeps the committed-value finding from firing on the `.env` in every README.

reference_scope.description: `episode`: 'nothing reads this' is claimed about the files in this episode only, and the finding says so at a lower confidence. `repo`: the caller supplied the repository's full reference set, which is the only basis for the confident version of the claim — and the card says out loud when `repo` was asked for and not given.

rename_similarity.description: Name-token similarity at which a removed variable and an added one are called one rename (`DATABASE_URL` → `PG_DATABASE_URL` shares 2 of 3 tokens). Low values merge unrelated removals into a rename; high values leave a half-done rename as two harmless-looking rows.

secret_name_pattern.description: Which variable names mean 'belongs in a secret store'. Deliberately a pattern, not a list: the useful part is the shape (`_KEY`, `TOKEN`, `DSN`), and every company has names the shape catches that a list does not.

findings.description: A variable this episode introduces, either declared in an env file or read by new code. The process environment is not in the repository, so nothing about the diff makes it exist in production.

ci_oidc_changed.description: `id-token: write`, a role ARN, an `environment:` binding or a vault login changed: the workflow can now mint an identity a cloud provider trusts. This is an access review, not a code review.

ci_permission_escalation.description: A `permissions:` block gained a write scope, or `write-all`. The token the job holds is now worth more than it was, and it is handed to every step in that job.

ci_runner_changed.description: A job moved onto a runner this project owns, or onto a new label. Everything the job can see — network, cache, credentials on the host — changed with it.

ci_secret_new.description: A workflow now reads `${{ secrets.X }}`. The build fails until somebody types that name into the repository, organisation or environment secrets — a fact nobody learns until a red tick.

ci_trigger_main_push.description: A `push` trigger that includes the default branch appeared, or a job gained one. Whatever that workflow does — publish, deploy, sign — now happens on merge.

container_base_changed.description: The `FROM` moved: a different vendor, a different major, or a different digest. Every binary in the image was built against the old one.

container_base_unpinned.description: No digest, or a tag that floats (`latest`, or no tag at all). The image you build next week is not the image you reviewed today.

container_privilege_changed.description: `USER root` added, the last non-root `USER` removed, `--privileged` or a capability granted. A container escape is now a root escape.

container_supply_chain.description: A `curl … | sh` in a Dockerfile: the build's reproducibility and the reviewer's threat model both now include whatever that server returns at build time.

deploy_coordination.description: The episode changes only durable-state surface: nothing here is safe to ship on the normal path, because there is no code for the migration to be compatible with.

env_added.description: A variable this episode introduces, either declared in an env file or read by new code. The process environment is not in the repository, so nothing about the diff makes it exist in production.

env_declared_unread.description: Declared in `.env.example` (or a ConfigMap, compose block or workflow `env:`) with no read found for it. Either the code that reads it has not landed, or the declaration is theatre and the operator will set a value that changes nothing.

env_removed.description: A variable that is no longer declared or read. Retiring it is the operator's job: a value left in a secret store with nothing reading it is a stale credential with an expiry nobody watches.

env_renamed.description: One variable removed and a similar one added in the same episode, with the old name still referenced. Renames are the failure mode of a diff-shaped tool: both halves look harmless alone.

env_stale_reference.description: The declaration is gone and a reference is not. This is the rename that was only half done: the process starts, reads nothing, and fails at the first request that needed it rather than at boot.

env_value_committed.description: A non-placeholder value for a secret-shaped name landed in a committed file. The value is now in every clone and every object the history holds.

flag_added.description: A new flag with the default value the code will see if the provider never answers. The default is the rollout plan whether the author meant it as one or not.

flag_default_changed.description: The default flipped. When the default is what ships, this diff *is* the rollout, and it happens to 100 % of traffic at the moment the deploy finishes.

flag_read_no_default.description: The call site supplies no fallback, so the provider is on the request path: a missing flag or a provider outage becomes the caller's problem.

flag_removed.description: A flag the code no longer reads, or a declaration that went while reads remained. Flag rows in a provider outlive the code that read them and confuse whoever inherits the panel.

iac_policy_widened.description: A new line widens an IAM policy, opens an ingress to the internet, or makes an instance public. The blast radius of this diff is not the repository.

iac_resource_added.description: A managed resource appeared in a plan. It costs money, has a name that must be globally unique, and will outlive the branch.

iac_resource_removed.description: A managed resource disappeared from the configuration, which in every IaC tool means *destroy it*. For a bucket, a table or a database that is the data, not the infrastructure.

migration_added.description: An ordered, execute-once change to durable state. It runs against a database that is still serving traffic, in an order the deploy has to get right.

migration_destructive.description: A `DROP`, `TRUNCATE`, `SET NOT NULL`, type change or rename in the forward path. These take locks, and some of them cannot be undone by anything.

migration_forward_only.description: A forward path with no down path: no `-- +goose Down`, no `def down`, no `.down.sql`, no undo script. A rollback of the release is now a manual repair with a different author.

migration_with_model.description: The schema file and the code that reads it move together, which is correct and also an ordering problem: one of the two will be true before the other.

flags.description: Files that declare flags with their defaults. Code that *reads* a flag is scanned wherever it lives, so this list only decides where defaults come from.

globs.description: Files that declare flags with their defaults. Code that *reads* a flag is scanned wherever it lives, so this list only decides where defaults come from.

require_default.description: Report a flag read that supplies no fallback. Off for a repository that runs its provider on the same node and treats a missing flag as a bug in the deploy.

iac.description: Infrastructure-as-code files: Terraform, CloudFormation, Kubernetes manifests, Helm values, Pulumi, Ansible. A manifest with `kind:` is also detected by content, because nothing about a path says a YAML file is a Deployment.

globs.description: Infrastructure-as-code files: Terraform, CloudFormation, Kubernetes manifests, Helm values, Pulumi, Ansible. A manifest with `kind:` is also detected by content, because nothing about a path says a YAML file is a Deployment.

widened_patterns.description: Text that widens an infrastructure exposure when it appears on an added line: a wildcard principal or action, a default route from anywhere, a public address.

migration.description: Migration layouts. The `e0.9`/`e2.1` taxonomy class `migration` is consulted first and these only add to it, so a repository with an unusual directory says it once.

destructive_ops.description: Statements treated as destroying or rewriting data in a forward path. Matched against statement text, case-insensitively, and extendable per repository.

globs.description: Migration layouts. The `e0.9`/`e2.1` taxonomy class `migration` is consulted first and these only add to it, so a repository with an unusual directory says it once.

model_globs.description: The model half of 'the migration and the model moved together': ORM definitions, `db/schema.rb`, `*.prisma`. Narrow on purpose — a Java package called `model` that moves without a migration is not a schema change.

patterns.description: Non-code surfaces a reviewer must be told about: config, env, flags, migrations and CI.

paths.description: The four paths Fathom writes to. Every relative path is resolved against the repository root and must stay inside it.

analysis_events.description: Append-only analysis event stream: what a run asked for, what each detector did, what every finding said, how the run ended (`e6.7`, docs/concepts/extensibility.md). Written only when `[events] enabled` is true; `fathom events` reads it back. A repo file may not point it outside the repository.

events.description: Append-only harness event stream the hook adapters write (ADR-005 §2).

objects.description: Content-addressed object directory for payloads too large to inline.

store.description: SQLite index + analysis cache. A relative path is resolved against the repository root; a value that escapes the root from a *repo* file is refused.

privacy.description: The runtime half of the no-network-by-default claim. Every key here is user-scoped: a clone may not consent on your behalf.

advisories.description: Consent to fetch security advisories (OSV). Off by default; needs the `net-advisories` feature to be compiled in as well.

llm.description: Consent for optional narrative polish. Off by default; the template is the degraded answer and is shipped as the good one.

mcp_http_transport.description: Consent to bind a network listener for MCP. A listener is as much a privacy decision as an outbound call, so it wears the same gate.

query.description: The interrupt budget for one store call on the keystroke path. Exceeding it is a stated partial, not a hang.

frame_store_budget_ms.description: One store call on the keystroke path may take this long before it is interrupted and rendered as a stated partial (ADR-004 §7.6).

ratchet.description: The baselined pre-existing violations graph.cycles reads. ADR-004 §5.1 declares `ratchet.` as an analyzer input, so the subtree exists here; `e3.10` may extend it, and the digest test refuses a silent absence.

baseline.description: The committed baseline of pre-existing violations (class M, ADR-004 §12). Committed on purpose: a baseline nobody can diff is a baseline nobody trusts.

mode.description: What a *new* violation above the baseline does: nothing, a finding, or a failing `fathom check` (exit 7). `warn` is the default because a ratchet that blocks a day-one review teaches nothing about the review.

rebuild.description: Free-disk-ratio required before a rebuild starts.

disk_ratio.description: Free-disk-to-store-size ratio required before a rebuild may start, so a rebuild cannot be the thing that fills the disk.

rename.description: Two questions with two bars. `rename.threshold` is what the diff pane prints as a rename; the `fact_bar`/`guess_floor` pair decides what the pairing engine asserts, what it labels a guess, and what it costs.

candidates.description: A source may claim its k best destinations and a destination its k best sources; a pair survives if either side wants it. This is what lets a 1-to-3 split be emitted at all — a 1:1 assignment cannot name three destinations at any threshold.

budget.description: Scored pairs per window before the candidate list is truncated to the best. Over budget is printed as a stated partial with the number dropped, never a silent short recall.

copies_harder.description: Widen copy sources to every path in the base tree — the only way to see a copy of a file nobody touched in this window. It is O(repo files), which `e2.4`'s own cost criterion rules out, and s4 priced what it buys: both real copies and fabricated pairings on a window where nothing moved. When on, every card prints the cost.

top_k.description: A source may claim its k best destinations and a destination its k best sources; a pair survives if either side wants it. This is what lets a 1-to-3 split be emitted at all — a 1:1 assignment cannot name three destinations at any threshold.

card.description: Rows per tier before the card names the remainder and the verb that lists it. A cap is not a truncation as long as the count survives — the auditor fails a card that loses rows silently.

rows.description: Rows per tier before the card names the remainder and the verb that lists it. A cap is not a truncation as long as the count survives — the auditor fails a card that loses rows silently.

content.description: Lines per shingle. One line is a bag of lines, which scores every file sharing an import header as similar — that is the decoy failure; three needs a run of context. Wider, and a moved-and-edited file stops matching at all.

min_shared_shingles.description: How many shingles two files must actually share before a similarity is a pairing. A four-line file sharing one shingle has a Jaccard of 1.00 and shares nothing worth calling provenance; without this floor every four-line config file is a candidate copy of every other.

normalise.description: `lines` folds whitespace only, so a moved-and-reformatted file is still found. `tokens` runs e2.2's token normaliser first, which makes a pure reformat invisible between the two blobs — and also erases the difference between two files that differ only in formatting, which a reviewer may want reported.

shingle_lines.description: Lines per shingle. One line is a bag of lines, which scores every file sharing an import header as similar — that is the decoy failure; three needs a run of context. Wider, and a moved-and-edited file stops matching at all.

copies.description: Let a file this window modified be a copy source. Still O(changed files), and the only copy a window-local method can ever see: a copy's source is never deleted, so a deletions-only source set is copy-blind by construction.

fact.description: Let the content matcher's own similarity assert a FACT at or above the fact bar. Off: a fact should be re-checkable with `git log --follow`, and s4 measured git's percentage as badly calibrated (ECE 0.182) once the engine pairs anything — worse for a number a reviewer cannot reproduce at all. On, and the row says the number is ours.

allow_content.description: Let the content matcher's own similarity assert a FACT at or above the fact bar. Off: a fact should be re-checkable with `git log --follow`, and s4 measured git's percentage as badly calibrated (ECE 0.182) once the engine pairs anything — worse for a number a reviewer cannot reproduce at all. On, and the row says the number is ours.

fact_bar.description: git's similarity index needed before a pairing is a FACT a reviewer is asked to act on. Measured on s4's corpus: at git's shipped 0.50 the engine asserts a named decoy and still misses every rewrite below R050; at 0.75 it ships nothing false. Every pairing below this bar is a labelled guess, because no threshold separates the corpus's decoy from its true rewrites.

folds.description: Let a file this window modified be a merge destination. Without it a fold into an existing module is invisible — the destination never appears among the additions, which is why git reports zero folds at any threshold.

guess_floor.description: The lowest-scoring guess the card prints. Not a correctness bar — no threshold removes the decoy — a display budget. 0.15 is the measured knee: every claimable pair the engine can find is found, and 0.10 buys two more (both above the claimable line) for three more rows and no fewer lies.

threshold.description: Similarity needed to call two paths the same file.

repo.description: The size class the budget defaults are chosen from.

size_class.description: Size class the budget defaults are read from. `auto` probes commit and file counts and takes the *stricter* of the two (ADR-004 §11.1); naming a class here is how you pay the xlarge budget on a machine that needs it.

retention.description: Windows on the live epoch. ADR-004 §8.2 states these numbers as `fathom.toml`'s `[retention]` defaults; they are restated here from that table and a test refuses drift.

blob_epochs.description: Blobs are small and deduplicated; the extra epoch is cheaper than the re-analysis it saves.

cache_epochs.description: Live epoch plus the one before, so an interrupted rebuild can be abandoned without losing the index it replaced.

index_run_keep_last.description: Index-run history is the §11 evidence trail.

store_event_days.description: Non-error store events age out; `error` rows are kept until read, because “when did it start happening” is the first question asked.

risk.description: The ranking knobs. Changing these changes `risk.score` and `delta.compose` and nothing else (ADR-004 §6).

tau.description: Risk threshold above which an episode is surfaced as needing attention. 70 until `e2.10`'s default was measured: nothing in 540 episodes of real OSS history reached it (`reco-6co`, docs/concepts/false-positive-calibration.md), so the confirmed default is the corpus's own top-decile floor.
